Reporting the software used to conduct the meta-analysis is important for several reasons. First, it allows other researchers to replicate the analysis and to verify the results. Second, it provides information about the capabilities and limitations of the software used, which can be helpful for other researchers when choosing software for their own meta-analyses. Third, it helps to ensure that the meta-analysis was conducted in a transparent and reproducible manner.

This practice enhances transparency and reproducibility in research, allowing readers to understand and potentially replicate the analysis. Providing information about the software used is also crucial for the scientific community to assess the validity of the findings and build upon the research in the future.
